cards.note: Debate: The 25 named prophets give a clear list players can check, and it avoids arguments over disputed figures.
Debate: Challenger's amendment. It makes 'Football Teams' clearer, and leaving out national teams stops the card from becoming the existing 'Countries' card (idx 10).
clearer wording; Debate: Adds the respectful ﷺ after the Prophet's mention and changes nothing else.

cards.Description: Urdu Muhavray and Kahawatein (Idioms and Proverbs)
cards.note: Debate: For Urdu speakers 'Urdu Words' never runs out, so no one ever fails. Muhavray (idioms) and kahawatein (proverbs) keep the card in Urdu, make it a real challenge and still have many well-known answers. The challenger's amended English gloss matches both terms.
Debate: Overlaps the live 'Pakistani Public Holidays' card (the Eids, 14 August, Milad). Once those are taken, only a handful of well-known answers are left.
too narrow (5 prayers); overlaps Types of Salah
Debate: Adds the everyday Urdu word. The answers are accurate and plentiful (the five daily prayers, Jumu'ah, Witr, Taraweeh, Tahajjud, Janazah, Istikhara, Eid...).
Debate: Ending arguments over whether desi ghee and banaspati count, which are staples of a Pakistani kitchen.
Debate: Uses the Pakistani/British spelling, consistent with other cards in the deck.

Restored: allowed by deck owner; Debate: Uses the term players know, makes clear there are many answers rather than just the anthem, and follows the deck's 'Mithai (Pakistani Sweets)' style. The owner allows milli naghmay.

clearer; Debate: 'Animals Found in Pakistan' nearly duplicates Animals (4). Limiting it to wild animals gives it its own answers: markhor, snow leopard, Indus dolphin, ibex, urial, chinkara, bears, jackal, mugger crocodile.
wording; Debate: Most people know only a handful of dams. Adding the real Indus barrages (Sukkur, Kotri, Guddu, Taunsa, Chashma, Jinnah, Panjnad) gives enough answers to play.

cards.Description: Famous Pakistani Schools and School Chains
cards.note: Debate: Stops players reading it as school types and points them to named schools (Beaconhouse, City School, Aitchison and so on). Matches 'Famous Pakistani Hospitals'.
designers too narrow/celebrity; brands widely known

cards.Description: Things You Hear at a Dhaba

cards.note: New card; Debate: Separates it from 'Pakistani Beverages'. In Pakistan a 'cold drink' means a soda, and there are plenty of brands to name.
New card; Debate: Removes the overlap with 'Things That Are Spicy' and follows the deck's existing 'Hard (Not Soft)' pattern.
Debate: Nearly the same card as School Supplies (129). Its other answers are covered by Things in a Lunch Box, Things in a Classroom and Things in an Exam Hall.

Things You See or Do When It Rains

cards.Description: Things You Get Sent to Buy From the Dukaan
cards.note: Debate: Near-duplicate of live 261 'Things at a Kiryana Store'; the answers (anday, doodh, double roti, cheeni, chai patti) are the same, so the round plays identically.

People Who Come to Your Door

cards.note: New card (debate): Accurate, with many well-known answers (Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Khaibar, Hunain, Yarmouk, Qadisiyyah, Hattin, Ain Jalut). Nothing like it is in the deck.

cards.Description: Occasions When We Say a Dua
cards.note: New card (debate): An everyday Islamic theme with many answers (eating, sleeping, travelling, leaving home, entering the masjid, after wudu). It is different from Good Deeds and Sunnah Habits.
New card (debate): Has about 10 well-known Pakistani answers (gajar, suji, besan, sohan, anday, badam, kaddu, chanay ki daal, habshi). It is not a duplicate of Mithai or Desserts.
New card (debate): A broad, easy card with many answers (pakoray, samosay, jalebi, puri, kachori, fries, fried fish, nimko). It is not a duplicate.
New card (debate): Relatable desi humour. It asks for items, not actions, so it does not duplicate 'Things You Do When Mehmaan Are Coming'.
New card (debate): Funny and relatable, with many answers (ice cream tubs, biscuit tins as sewing boxes, shopping bags, jam jars, old shirts as pochay). Nothing like it is in the deck.

cards.Description: Rooms and Parts of a House
cards.note: New card (debate): Has many answers (sehan, chhat, verandah, drawing room, store, garage, balcony, staircase). The existing room cards ask for objects, not rooms.
New card (debate): The colour series has Green, Yellow, Red, White, Black, Blue and Brown but no Orange. Easy answers: kinnow, carrot, papaya, jalebi, marigold, Fanta, tiger.
New card (debate): A new property card with plenty of local answers (gas cylinder, deg, almirah, fridge, sack of wheat, truck). Not in the deck.

New card (debate): The challenger's version of P7. Leaving out animals stops it from turning into the Animals card and keeps the household-object spirit of the With Buttons/Handles/Holes cards: charpai, chair, table, stool, takht, ironing stand, tripod, peerhi.
New card (debate): A household-object card with a local feel (pateela, pressure cooker, tiffin, deg, kettle, achaar jar, thermos). Different from Things You Can Fill With Water.
New card (debate): An easy, funny property card (gold, mirror, bangles, steel utensils, coins, new Eid shoes, a bald head). Not in the deck.

cards.Description: Restaurants and Food Chains in Pakistan
cards.note: New card (debate): The challenger's version of P10. It gives players in every city answers (KFC, McDonald's, Savour Foods, Student Biryani, OPTP, Broadway, Cheezious, Kababjees, Bundu Khan) and drops Monal Islamabad, which was demolished in 2024. Different from Fast Food Items and Pakistani Brands.
New card (debate): New shape category (deck has only Round and Shapes); many everyday answers like tiles, carrom board, ludo board, chessboard, napkin and window.
New card (debate): Fits the Ammi Says/Abbu Says family-humour series; no Dadi card exists and Dadi lines have their own flavour.
New card (debate): Counterpart to Things That Smell Good with many clean answers (garbage, rotten eggs, fish market, burnt food, diesel smoke).
New card (debate): Familiar Pakistani market setting; challenger's amendment uses 'Sunday Bazaar', the name used across the country, instead of the regional 'Itwar' with a clumsy gloss.
New card (debate): Completes the Dishes Made With series; many answers (keema matar, aloo keema, karela keema, keema naan, samosa, kofta, seekh kebab, cutlets).

cards.Description: Excuses for Leaving a Dawat Early
cards.note: New card (debate): New local, family-friendly excuses angle that does not duplicate the late/homework excuse cards.
New card (debate): Sensory category with many answers (crickets, dogs barking, chowkidar's whistle, generator, AC, mosquitoes, horns); distinct from Things You Hear at a Dhaba.

cards.Description: Things You Do Before Going to Sleep
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday routine not covered in the deck; many answers including Islamic ones (wudu, Ayat ul Kursi, the Three Quls, dusting the bed).

cards.Description: Things That Are Furry or Hairy
cards.note: New card (debate): New texture category; many answers (cat, sheep, teddy bear, beard, moustache, carpet, blanket, coconut, kiwi).
New card (debate): The deck has other colour cards but none for pink. Players have many everyday answers: gulab, falooda, Rooh Afza milk, buddhi ke baal, flamingo.
New card (debate): No purple card exists. Plenty of local answers: baingan, jamun, falsa, angoor, aloo bukhara, chukandar, kaali gajar.

cards.Description: Dishes Made With Gosht (Mutton or Beef)
cards.note: New card (debate): Completes the 'Dishes Made With' set (Aloo, Anday, Chicken, Qeema, Dahi). Huge answer pool: nihari, haleem, paye, korma, karahi, sajji, pulao.

cards.Description: Things You Do in the Morning
cards.note: New card (debate): Pairs with 'Things You Do Before Going to Sleep' without duplicating it or 'Things That Wake You Up'. Universal answers: Fajr, chai, brushing teeth, paratha.
New card (debate): Fits the deck's object-property cards and overlaps only partly with 'Things Made of Glass'. Answers include anday, crockery, mobile screens, biscuits, pencil lead.

cards.Description: Excuses for Not Answering the Phone
cards.note: New card (debate): The answers differ from the existing excuse cards (late, homework, dawat) and are relatable and funny: battery dead, phone on silent, in namaz, no signal.

New card (debate): Counterpart to 'Things That Are Soft'. '(Not Soft)' makes the physical meaning clear. The challenger's 'Hard to Touch' would mean 'difficult to touch' and make the card harder to understand.
New card (debate): No besan card exists (only Atta or Maida); fits the ingredient series with many answers such as pakoray, kadhi, besan ki roti, ladoo, boondi and cheela.
New card (debate): Not a duplicate. 'Pulses (Daals)' asks for the pulses themselves, while this card asks for dishes: cholay, chana chaat, chana pulao, haleem, hummus and falafel.
New card (debate): Completes the texture set alongside Hard, Soft and Sticky. The answers are clear (marble, glass, tiles, silk, phone screen).

cards.Description: Excuses for Missing School or Office
cards.note: New card (debate): Different from the existing excuse cards (being late, homework, dawat, phone). It is relatable and has many answers.

cards.Description: Things You Do When You Get Home
cards.note: New card (debate): Pairs with the morning routine card and has many everyday answers. No duplicate found in the deck.
New card (debate): Texture companion to Smooth/Soft/Hard/Sticky; not in deck; many everyday answers (jhaanwa, sandpaper, bark, brick, cracked heels).
New card (debate): Pairs with 'Things That Are Heavy' and matches the deck's 'Things That Are Hard (Not Soft)' wording; broad answer pool.
New card (debate): Fits the 'Dishes Made With...' series; 'Pulses (Daals)' lists only daal types, not dishes (daal chawal, haleem, khichri, dahi baray, daal gosht, moong daal halwa).

cards.Description: Excuses for Not Lending Someone Money
cards.note: New card (debate): Relatable, family-safe and different from the existing excuse cards.

cards.Description: Excuses for Not Helping With Housework
cards.note: New card (debate): Challenger's amendment: broader and more local than room-cleaning (shared rooms, Ammi's chores and errands), and separate from the existing excuse cards and 'Household Chores'.

cards.Description: Things You Check Before Leaving the House
cards.note: New card (debate): Not in the deck and different from 'Things You Find in Your Pocket' and 'Things People Lose'; enough answers (keys, wallet, phone, gas stove, iron, lights, taps, locks).

cards.Description: Things You Do on a Day Off
cards.note: New card (debate): Broad and easy; goes with the morning and get-home routine cards, and nothing like it is in the deck.
New card (debate): Not in deck. A broad, easy property category (wuzu hands, mop, fresh laundry, fish, sponge) that fits beside Rough/Soft/Sticky/Hard and reaches well beyond the rain card.
New card (debate): Not in deck. Plenty of everyday answers (rubber band, naala, chewing gum, pizza cheese, balloon, hair tie, socks).
New card (debate): Not in deck. Very relatable for Pakistani households (haldi, chai, mehndi, achaar oil, paan, ink, shoe polish).
New card (debate): Not in deck. Familiar, funny answers (roof in barsaat, tanki, tap, pen, geyser, AC, runny nose) and no overlap with existing cards.

cards.Description: Excuses for Skipping a Walk or Exercise
cards.note: New card (debate): None of the deck's several 'Excuses for ...' cards covers exercise. Many funny answers (too hot, smog, ate too much, will start Monday).
New card (debate): Fits the Things Made of Wood/Glass/Paper/Metal/Plastic/Cloth series and has many everyday answers (matka, surahi, diya, gamla, kulhar, handi, tandoor, eent, gullak).

New card (debate): Fills a gap in the Dishes Made With ... series. Its answers are dishes, unlike Milk Products (81): kheer, firni, rabri, kulfi, sheer khurma, seviyan, ras malai, custard, doodh patti.

New card (debate): Distinct from Islamic Terms (42) and Occasions When We Say a Dua (386). Every player knows many accurate answers (Assalamu Alaikum, MashaAllah, InshaAllah, JazakAllah, SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Astaghfirullah).
New card (debate): A familiar local theme with many answers, including non-food goods (balloons, toys, chooriyan). It is distinct from Pakistani Street Food (93) and Sunday Bazaar.

cards.Description: Gifts People Bring Back From Umrah or Hajj
cards.note: New card (debate): Accurate, well-known answers (Aab-e-Zamzam, khajoor, tasbeeh, jai namaz, attar, topi, miswak, surma). It is different from Things You See on Umrah (268).
New card (debate): A fun ingredient card like Things You Put in Chaat (321), with non-spice answers (aloo, alu bukhara, dahi, piyaz, kewra, zafran) that set it apart from Spices (8).
New card (debate): A relatable household card with many answers, different from 'Bedroom Items' and not already in the deck.
New card (debate): A new property card with many answers. It overlaps only a little with 'Things Made of Glass'.
New card (debate): An open shape card with many answers, different from 'Tall' and not already in the deck.
New card (debate): Nostalgic for families, with enough well-known answers (marbles, stamps, wrappers, cricket cards, coins, stickers); not in the deck.
New card (debate): Everyone knows the answers (feeder, Cerelac, jhoola, chusni, pram); not in the deck and different from 'Baby Animals'.
New card (debate): A funny local card with many recognisable lines; not in the deck.

cards.Description: Things You Do on a Long Car Journey
cards.note: New card (debate): A relatable family-trip card, different from 'Things You Pack for Travel' and 'Things in Abbu's Car'.

New card (debate): I took the challenger's amended version: adding the well-known gully rules gives a bigger answer pool than catchphrases alone. It stays different from 'Cricket Terms' and 'Things at a Cricket Match'.
New card (debate): Not in the deck, and players can name plenty (cement, eent, bajri, sariya, mistri, crane, mixer, helmet). Follows the deck's 'Things at a ...' pattern.

cards.Description: Things at a School Sports Day
cards.note: New card (debate): A shared Pakistani memory with many answers (sack race, lemon-spoon race, tug of war, march past, medals). 'Sports' and 'Things in a Playground' do not cover it.
New card (debate): A new local setting with many answers (FIR, constable, SHO, lockup, wardi, danda). Within the content rules.
New card (debate): Distinct from 143 'Pakistani Government Departments' (department names) and 'Things at a Bank'. Relatable answers (files, stamps, queues, clerk, 'kal aana').
New card (debate): Not in the deck, and different from 'Bedroom Items' because of the student-life answers (warden, mess, roommate, bunk bed, kettle).
New card (debate): A common urban setting that is not in the deck, with many answers (escalator, food court, trial room, ATM, parking).

cards.Description: Things You See on a Trip to the Northern Areas
cards.note: New card (debate): A very common Pakistani trip. The card asks for things seen (jeeps, glaciers, yaks, landslides, KKH), not the places covered by the 'Valleys', 'Lakes' and 'Hill Stations' cards.

cards.Description: Things You Find Under the Sofa or Bed
cards.note: New card (debate): No similar card in the deck, and it has many everyday answers (remote, coins, socks, chappal, charger, toys, pen, dust).

cards.Description: Things Students Do the Night Before an Exam
cards.note: New card (debate): This card is about what students do, while Things in an Exam Hall lists objects in a place, so they don't overlap. It has many relatable answers.
New card (debate): A broad category that is not in the deck yet. Jinn and ghost answers are allowed by the owner.

New card (debate): The owner allows video games, and Board Games and Pakistani Traditional Games are different categories. Many well-known answers (PUBG, Free Fire, Ludo Star, Candy Crush, FIFA, Minecraft, Subway Surfers, Tekken).

New card (debate): The owner allows social media, and the answers differ from Pakistani Apps and Websites (WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, YouTube, Telegram, X, Imo, Signal, LinkedIn).

cards.Description: Things People Do at a Dawat
cards.note: New card (debate): No card covers what people do at a dawat; the existing dawat-related cards list objects, places or excuses. Many relatable answers.

New card (debate): Fits the deck's cards about object features (Handles, Lids, Buttons) and has plenty of answers (bags, jackets, purses, wallets, suitcases, pencil boxes, cushion covers, tents, jeans, hoodies).
New card (debate): About 50 answers that suit the audience. It is a narrower, harder version of 'Countries', not a copy of it, and no such card exists.
New card (debate): Many well-known, accurate answers (Salahuddin, Muhammad bin Qasim, Tariq bin Ziyad, Mehmed II, Tipu Sultan, the Mughals, Ghaznavi). Nothing in the deck covers this.
New card (debate): A fresh word-pattern card with plenty of real answers (Islamabad, Faisalabad, Hyderabad, Abbottabad, Jacobabad, Muzaffarabad, Nazimabad...).

cards.Description: English Words Used in Everyday Urdu
cards.note: New card (debate): Hundreds of answers everyone knows, and it fits alongside the Punjabi, Pashto and Sindhi Words cards.
New card (debate): Challenger's amendment. It keeps the fun idea, follows the deck's 'English (Roman Urdu)' title pattern, and does not give away answers in the title.
New card (debate): Grouping by cooking method mixes breads and meats, so the answers differ enough from Bread Types and Types of Kebabs. There are plenty of answers.
New card (debate): Many everyday answers (khussa, belt, wallet, jacket, cricket ball, sofa), and the material is not yet in the deck's 'Things Made of...' set.
